activities.label: Big picture map
activities.title: Europe before 1914
activities.body: Read the map and get the overall picture first.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions shaped a divided Europe before 1914.

activities.label: Say it back
activities.title: What made Europe tense?
activities.body: In your own words, explain the main prewar tension pattern and one tension it created.
activities.correctAnswer: Europe was split into rival alliance blocs, and those rivalries made the continent tense before 1914.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names the rival blocs and explains that the tension made a larger war easier to start.

activities.label: Fix the sequence
activities.title: From Sarajevo to war
activities.body: Use the feedback to correct the outbreak sequence in one clear attempt.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Mixing up the assassination, the July Crisis, and the war declarations as one single event instead of a chain.
activities.concept: Sequence from the Sarajevo assassination to declarations of war
activities.correctAnswer: Sarajevo assassination, July Crisis, ultimatums and mobilization, then declarations of war.
activities.feedback: The key repair is that Sarajevo started the chain, but war came only after the diplomatic crisis and mobilization steps.

activities.label: Timeline from memory
activities.title: WWI timeline in order
activities.body: Explain the basic 1914 to 1918 chronology without looking back.
activities.feedback: A complete answer places the war's start before U.S. entry and the armistice last.

choices: Sarajevo assassination, July Crisis, declarations of war

activities.feedback: The correct sequence is the one that keeps the assassination first, the crisis next, and the war declarations after that.
